finding: adopt writes the owner record in place with write_text (truncate then write) while add_owner's lookup reads each record without the lock; a read in the gap sees a truncated file and add_owner skips the record
why: add_owner then answers None for a worktree that has a record, so the started agent is never added to the owners and a prune can judge the worktree dead; the lock added in this delta does not cover add_owner's unlocked probe read. (also raised by delta-sweep)
fix: Write through a scratch file and os.replace, as add_owner does at worktree_owner.py:248-251.
evidence: record_file.write_text(json.dumps(record), encoding="utf-8")  vs  worktree_owner.py:236-239 `with open(path) as handle: document = json.load(handle) except ValueError: continue` (outside record_lock)

finding: The new token-checked lock release has no test: no test makes the holder's lock be replaced by another holder's lock and shows the first holder leaves it.
why: The delta adds the token so a slow holder never deletes a successor's lock; unconditional os.remove(lock) in the finally block would pass every test in test_worktree_owner.py.
fix: Add a test that replaces the lock file with a different token inside the `with record_lock(...)` body and asserts the lock file still exists with the other token after exit.
evidence: if _read(lock) == token:  (finally block of record_lock); tests added: test_add_owner_gives_up_after_waiting_for_a_held_record_lock (record_lock raises before the yield, so the finally never runs), test_a_stale_takeover_that_moved_a_fresh_lock_gives_it_back (calls _take_if_stale only)

finding: _take_if_stale reads the lock content (the 'judged' snapshot) after the mtime staleness check, so a fresh lock that replaced the stale one in between is judged as stale and deleted
why: The give-back only works when judged holds the stale holder's content; here judged can already hold the fresh holder's token, so `_read(grave) != judged` is false and the fresh lock is removed while its holder is inside the critical section. (also raised by delta-sweep)
fix: Read the content first, then check the mtime, then rename; or after the rename test os.path.getmtime(grave) against LOCK_STALE (rename keeps mtime) and give back when fresh.
evidence: if time.time() - os.path.getmtime(lock) <= LOCK_STALE: return ... judged, grave = _read(lock), ... os.rename(lock, grave) ... if _read(grave) != judged: (interleaving: P1 getmtime sees stale L; P2 renames+removes L; P3 creates fresh L'; P1 _read(L)=L' token=judged; P1 renames L' to grave; grave==judged so P1 removes it; P3 still holds, P4 can acquire). The new test hides this by stubbing _read to return the stale text.

fix: Also refuse agent_id == CONTACT in agent_start, with a test beside the -sup one.

finding: NameTaken names sorted(names)[0], the first of the entry's own names, not the name the other entry holds
why: When only one of the entry's two names collides, the reason quotes the wrong string, and that reason reaches the exit-4 answer the contact agent reads. (also raised by delta-sweep)
fix: Quote the colliding name: sorted(names & {other['pane_label'], other['agent_name']})[0].
evidence:
if names & {other["pane_label"], other["agent_name"]}:
    raise NameTaken(f"agent {other['agent_id']} already holds the name {sorted(names)[0]!r}")

finding: test_a_name_lost_5_times_answers_exit_4_and_starts_nothing does not count the attempts, so the 5-try cap that D-146 decides is not pinned.
why: The stub raises NameTaken on every call; a loop of 1 or 2 tries ends in the same exit 4 and passes.
fix: Count the calls to the stubbed record_entry and assert the count equals 5.
evidence: assert code == 4 and "a9" in body["reason"] and "agent-start" not in team.transport.verbs()  (D-146: "agent-start takes the next name on that refusal, 5 tries")

finding: record_lock creates the lock file, then writes the token; an OSError on the write leaves an empty lock that nothing removes
why: The old os.open/os.close pair had no write step; now a failed write (disk full) propagates before the try/finally, so every other writer waits until LOCK_STALE (30 s) and then LOCK_WAIT (10 s) expires with an OSError.
fix: Wrap the token write in try/except OSError and os.remove(lock) before re-raising.
evidence:
with open(lock, "x", encoding="utf-8") as out:
    out.write(token)
 break   (the try: yield / finally: remove starts only after the loop)
